timeline.line: This is Data Lens. It catches workforce health risk before the shift starts, not after someone gets hurt.
At a Gulf port in July, crews work through thirty five degree nights, often several in a row. The warning signs already exist. They sit in six different systems, and get reviewed after the fact.
Data Lens joins them up. It scores tomorrow's roster, spots trouble days ahead, and keeps health detail with the clinic.
The planner scores tomorrow's roster in one click. A hundred and sixty six people, each against their own job. Three should do something else tonight.
Marco is one of them. The reasons are in work terms: a third night in a row, short sleep, and broken cooling in his camp. Never a diagnosis.
Data Lens proposes ground work, with his own crew. The planner accepts. The shift manager approves. Two people, one log.
Days ahead, the head of safety sees Camp Block C on watch. Clinic heat visits and cooling faults both rose. Two kinds of signal agree, so a warning opens before anyone is hurt.
The copilot drafts each step, and a person confirms it. The fix: repair eleven cooling units, with an owner and a date.
Marco gets the change on his phone, in Filipino. Then a three tap check-in: sleep, how he feels, and water.
During the shift, the deck sensor stays above thirty two degrees. The foreman gets one instruction: change the work and rest cycle. One tap to confirm.
A worker feels unwell. Two taps, and the clinic knows. The permit log records it, without a name.
Only the clinician sees health detail. She records Marco's outcome, and Marco decides if his employer sees it. The outcome, never the reason.
The copilot follows the same rules. A planner asks for lab results, and it says no.
The district health authority sees totals across employers. Any group under ten is hidden.
Does it work? On ninety days of history with four hidden events, it caught all four, at least seventy four hours early.
What we built in this challenge is a working product. Roster scoring, early warning, a worker phone app, clinic only health data, eight role views, and nearly three hundred automated tests.
